title: Surrogate-Assisted Estimation of Exposure-Time Effects in Stepped-Wedge Trials with Administratively Censored Outcomes
summary: In stepped-wedge trials, effects often change with the time since a cluster crossed over, and a delayed primary outcome is administratively censored for clusters that cross over late. The design couples them: long exposure times occur only in the last periods, where censoring is heaviest. We study exposure-time-specific effects when a short-term surrogate is always recorded and censoring is ignorable given the surrogate, exposure time, covariates and calendar time.
